•424. SHRIMATI SARLA MAHESHWARI: Will the Minister of CIVIL 
AVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) what is the number of projects pending with the Central Government 
for clearance, State-wise; 
(b) what is the duration of their pendency, project-wise; and 
(c) what are the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SYED SHAHNAWAZ

indicated below:

Interest rates on deposits in Urban Co-operative Banks 
*427. SHRI YADLAPATI VENKAT RAO: Will the Minister of FINANCE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Reserve Bank of India has issued a directive to the 
Urban Co-operative Banks to slash the interest rates on deposits to 
the level offered by the commercial banks; 
(b) if so, the rate of interest  Urban Co-operative Banks were 
paying before the directive of the RBI; and 
(c) what is the rate of interest of commercial banks at present? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI 
BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL): (a) and (b) Urban cooperative banks are free 
to determine their rate of interest on term 
8 

[23 April, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
deposits with the approval of their Board of Directors. However, offering 
high rate of interest which is not in alignment with market rates, affects the 
profitability of banks and adds to their liability. Therefore, Urban 
cooperative banks were advised by RBI in January 2002 to review their 
interest rate structure on term depos its of different maturities and take 
appropriate action to make them comp arable with the rates offered by 
commercial banks. 
(c) With effect from October 22, 1997, RBI has given freedom to 
commercial banks to fix their own interest rates on domestic term deposits of 
various maturities. At present the term deposit rates of different banks are 
generally between 8% to 9% p.a. Howeve r, interest rate on savings deposits 
is still regulated by RBI and this rate has been fixed at 4.0 per cent per 
annum since April 1, 2000.

*431. SHRI SANJAY NIRUPAM: Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Air India has made any profit for the year 2001-2002; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether Air India has made any profit from non-operating revenue or its 
unutilised bilateral rights; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SYED SHAHNAWAZ 
HUSSAIN): (a) and (b) Air India has earned a net profit of Rs. 4.71 crores 
during the period April, 2001 to January, 2002. Based on Traffic trends during

*432. SHRI B. J. PANDA: Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the export growth target has been slashed by 12 per cent for the 
current fiscal year as against the previously achieved growth rate of 19.83 per 
cent in 2000-2001; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; 
(c) the country's targeted International share (in terms of 
percentage) for 2000-2001; 
(d) the share (in terms of percentage) of "ores and minerals" in India's total 
export in 2000-2001 and the projection for the current year; and 
(e) whether any study is made to qualify the improvement in export 
growth rate by exporting value added products of these "ores and minerals" 
instead of exporting them as it is? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI MURASOLI 
MAR AN): (a) and (b) Keeping in view the global ec onomic slowdown and 
events of September 11 and their aftermath, the annual export target was scaled down 
to 3% from 12% which was originally envisaged at the beginning of 2001-02. Export 
growth rate achieved during 2000-01 was 21% which was the highest growth rate 
in the last decade. 
(c) As per WTO Report, share of India's merchandise export is 
0.67% during 2000. 
(d) As per the data available from Directorate General of 
Commercial Intelligence and Statistics (DGCI&S), Calcutta, the 
export of ores and minerals accounted  for 2.61% share in total export 
during 2000-01. Export of minerals and ores sector is projected to be 
around US $ 1497 million in the financial year (2001-2002). 
(e) No formal study has been conducted specifically on the issue of 
improving export growth rate by exporting value added products 
rather than ores and minerals in their raw form.
